rawCommits.subject: fix(left-menu): restore right-click context menu in LeftMenuTree (#74)
rawCommits.body:
The projects sidebar was migrated from the legacy ListItem-based tree to
LeftMenuTree, but `useExplorerMenus` still resolves the clicked row via
`closest("[data-list-item][id]")`. LeftMenuTree rows render `id={entry.id}`
yet never emit the `data-list-item` marker, so the selector never matches:
`handleContextMenu` (and the F2-rename `handleKeyDown`) bail out early. As a
result, right-click in the projects sidebar (Remove from Project, Rename,
Add Agent, Delete Project) and F2-to-rename silently do nothing.

Add `data-list-item=""` to both LeftMenuTree row buttons — the leaf/agent
rows and the project/section group headers — so the existing selector
matches and the context menu + keyboard rename can resolve the node again.
`agentMeta` already includes archived agents, so this also restores the
delete path for archived agents.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: restore right-click context menu in LeftMenuTree (#74)

rawCommits.subject: Add usage signal analytics with billing enrichment (#75)
rawCommits.body:
Adds a pure usage-signal classifier plus server-side emission for completed chat turns, persisted as turn_usage_signal and sent to Mixpanel as agent_turn_classified.

Enriches the signal from z-billing account data with account age, funding buckets, grant usage buckets, lifetime purchased/granted/used cents, and balance fields.

Verified with cargo test -p aura-os-usage-signals; cargo test -p aura-os-server usage_signal; cargo test -p aura-os-server --test chat_events_test bare_agent_chat_route_persists_usage_signal_from_harness_end; cargo test -p aura-os-server mixpanel; npm --prefix interface run test -- src/lib/analytics-contract.test.ts; cargo clippy -p aura-os-usage-signals -- -D warnings; cargo clippy -p aura-os-server --tests -- -D warnings -A clippy::derivable_impls -A clippy::items_after_test_module.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: Add usage signal analytics with billing enrichment (#75)

rawCommits.subject: fix(models): drop unsupported 'minimal' reasoning effort from GPT-5.4 family
rawCommits.body:
GPT-5.4 / -mini / -nano reject reasoning_effort=minimal (their native
set is none/low/medium/high/xhigh), unlike GPT-5.5 which keeps minimal.
The picker offered minimal and gpt-5.4-nano even defaulted to it, so
every nano call 400'd. Add a GPT_5_4_EFFORTS (low/medium/high) set,
apply it to the 5.4 family, and flip nano's default to low. Persisted
'minimal' self-heals via the existing efforts validation.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: drop unsupported 'minimal' reasoning effort from GPT-5.4 family

rawCommits.subject: fix(model-picker): stop hover flyouts stacking when the menu scrolls
rawCommits.body:
Scrolling the model list under a stationary pointer surfaced new rows
that each opened their flyout; the single-open coordinator closed the
previous one, but that row's still-attached scroll-reflow listener fired
in the same scroll event and re-opened it, stacking multiple submenus
(reported as overlapping panels in the picker).

Track open/closed intent in a synchronous ref so a stale reflow on an
already-closed flyout bails instead of resurrecting it. The flyout still
repositions live while genuinely open. Adds regression tests for the
single-open invariant and the close-then-scroll race.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: stop hover flyouts stacking when the menu scrolls

rawCommits.subject: fix(stream): stop the stuck-stream watchdog from killing live turns
rawCommits.body:
The client-side watchdog hard-aborted a chat turn (onStop → cancel-turn)
after 60s of wire silence. On long extended-thinking turns the stream can
legitimately go quiet past 60s, so this abandoned turns that were still
alive — and since the upstream completes and bills regardless, the user
was charged for a turn the UI showed as failed.

The destructive 60s abort also pre-empted the graceful recovery path: a
genuine socket drop is caught by the 90s SSE idle reattach
(SSEIdleTimeoutError, recoverable), which re-attaches to the still-running
turn instead of cancelling it.

Move the destructive auto-abort from 60s to a 5-minute absolute safety cap
(FULLY_TIMED_OUT_MS -> ABSOLUTE_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000). The non-destructive
30s "stuck" pill (Stop / Retry / Report) is unchanged and remains the
"taking longer than usual" affordance; the hard abort now fires only after
genuinely-dead total silence (no heartbeat and no successful reattach).
Not killing a live turn also means the user receives the output they were
billed for.

Adds a regression test pinning that the abort no longer fires at the old
60s mark (only at the cap), and strengthens the partial-image guard to
walk past the new cap so it still proves markStreamProgress resets the
clock.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: stop the stuck-stream watchdog from killing live turns

rawCommits.subject: fix(remote-agents): stop polling state of dead/stuck remote agents
rawCommits.body:
When a remote agent failed to provision (e.g. K8s pod unschedulable) or
got stuck, the frontend kept polling GET /api/agents/{id}/remote_agent/state
forever — 30s app-wide from the profile-status store plus 2.5s from the
AgentEnvironment popover — each returning 502/404. A failed agent left open
flooded the console with hundreds of failed requests over many minutes and
hammered the server + swarm gateway for no benefit.

Make the pollers give up gracefully:
- profile-status-store: stop polling once an agent reports a terminal state
  (error/stopped) or fails MAX_CONSECUTIVE_POLL_FAILURES (3) times in a row,
  keeping its last status. Re-arm via the RemoteAgentStateChanged WS push
  (recovery) or a later registerRemoteAgents list refresh.
- useRemoteAgentVm / useRemoteAgentState: back off the recursive poll to a
  60s settled interval on terminal/repeated-failure, and auto-resume when a
  later poll succeeds.

The provisioning -> ready happy path is unchanged (provisioning keeps the
fast cadence; a successful poll resets the failure counter). No server
change — transport errors are still surfaced rather than masked.

Adds tests for terminal-state pause, consecutive-failure pause, WS
re-engagement, and the popover back-off cadence.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: stop polling state of dead/stuck remote agents

rendered.title: Sturdier streams, smarter pollers, and a refreshed model lineup
rendered.intro: Today's nightly is a reliability-leaning release: long-running chat turns are no longer killed by an over-eager watchdog, dead remote agents stop hammering the backend, and the model picker behaves itself when scrolled. Alongside the fixes, three new Fireworks-hosted models land in the catalog and a new server-side usage-signal pipeline begins emitting enriched analytics for completed chat turns.

entries.title: Projects sidebar regains right-click and F2 rename
entries.summary: Restores the context menu and keyboard-rename actions that silently broke after the sidebar's migration to LeftMenuTree.

items.text: Right-click actions (Remove from Project, Rename, Add Agent, Delete Project) and F2-to-rename work again in the projects sidebar — LeftMenuTree rows now emit the `data-list-item` marker that `useExplorerMenus` relies on to resolve the clicked node, which also re-enables deletion of archived agents.

entries.title: Server-side usage-signal analytics for chat turns
entries.summary: A new classifier emits an enriched `agent_turn_classified` event for each completed chat turn, persisted as `turn_usage_signal` and forwarded to Mixpanel.

items.text: Introduces a dedicated `aura-os-usage-signals` crate and server-side emission path that classifies completed chat turns with context like route kind, agent binding source, plan mode, council, cross-agent origin, attachment count, and project layout.

Enriches every signal with z-billing account data — account age, funding and grant-usage buckets, lifetime purchased/granted/used cents, and balance — so downstream analytics can segment turns by billing posture.

entries.title: Model catalog refresh: new Fireworks models and a GPT-5.4 effort fix
entries.summary: Adds three Fireworks-hosted chat models and corrects an effort-set mismatch that was 400-ing every GPT-5.4 nano call.

items.text: Adds Kimi K2.7 Code (256K), GLM 5.2 (1M), and Qwen3.7 Plus (256K) to the catalog with matching display pricing, legacy-id aliases, and benchmark-pricing mirror entries.

Stops the picker from offering `minimal` reasoning effort on GPT-5.4 / -mini / -nano (their API rejects it) and flips nano's default to `low`, so requests no longer 400; persisted `minimal` self-heals via the existing efforts validation.

entries.title: Model picker no longer stacks overlapping flyouts on scroll
entries.summary: Fixes a race where scrolling the model list under a stationary pointer left multiple submenus open at once.

items.text: Tracks open/closed intent in a synchronous ref so a stale scroll-reflow on an already-closed flyout bails instead of resurrecting it, preserving the single-open invariant while keeping live repositioning intact; regression tests pin both the invariant and the close-then-scroll race.

entries.title: Stuck-stream watchdog stops killing live chat turns
entries.summary: The destructive 60s auto-abort that was cancelling long extended-thinking turns — and billing users for output they never saw — is replaced with a 5-minute absolute safety cap.

items.text: Raises the destructive auto-abort from 60s to a 5-minute `ABSOLUTE_TIMEOUT_MS` cap so long extended-thinking turns aren't cancelled mid-flight; the 90s SSE idle reattach can now recover real socket drops instead of being pre-empted, and users actually receive the output they were billed for.

The non-destructive 30s "taking longer than usual" pill (Stop / Retry / Report) is unchanged; new tests pin that the abort no longer fires at the old 60s mark and that `markStreamProgress` keeps the watchdog quiet across the new window.

entries.title: Remote-agent pollers back off on dead or stuck VMs
entries.summary: Failed or unschedulable remote agents no longer flood `/remote_agent/state` with hundreds of 502/404s.

items.text: The profile-status store stops polling once an agent reports a terminal `error`/`stopped` state or fails three polls in a row, then re-arms via the `RemoteAgentStateChanged` websocket push or a later `registerRemoteAgents` refresh.

The AgentEnvironment popover's recursive poll backs off from its 2.5s provisioning cadence to a 60s settled interval on terminal or repeatedly-failing states, and auto-resumes the fast cadence when a poll succeeds again — leaving the provisioning→ready happy path untouched.

highlights: Long extended-thinking turns no longer get auto-killed at 60s
Dead remote agents stop flooding the backend with state polls
Kimi K2.7 Code, GLM 5.2, and Qwen3.7 Plus join the model catalog
GPT-5.4 nano calls no longer 400 on unsupported 'minimal' effort
